summary: Backend-only validation of the new Telegram copy-trading module + regression on existing endpoints. Added /app/backend/tests/test_telegram_copy.py with 26 new pytest tests. Full backend suite: 91/91 PASSED in 56.76s (65 previous + 26 new). All target features verified against LOCAL backend (http://localhost:8001). Telegram routes exist, return correct shape, are auth-gated (401 without JWT), config persists across GET/POST partial updates, and the LLM-based parser (Claude Sonnet 4.5 via emergentintegrations) correctly handles: (1) RentaTrade format with entry range + runner TP, (2) non-signal chat, (3) SELL with GOLD->XAUUSD alias. Backend stayed responsive even though Telethon cannot reach Telegram from sandbox (AuthKeyUnregisteredError in logs is EXPECTED per the agent-to-agent context note). No regression: /api/health, /api/auth/login, /api/bot/state, /api/positions/open, /api/trades/metrics, /api/mt5/status all still 200.

minor.issue: On sandbox returns 500 with 'AuthKeyUnregisteredError' because Telethon cannot reach Telegram MTProto. This is documented as EXPECTED in the review request (agent_to_agent_context_note). Auth-gate test (401 without JWT) passes — the endpoint itself is correctly wired. Not a bug, just to be aware on the VPS.
Cosmetic: 'AttributeError: module bcrypt has no attribute __about__' still in logs (login works). Same as previous iterations, pin bcrypt<4 to silence.

action_items: Nothing blocking — Telegram copy-trading module is fully functional on the backend side (parser, config, signals listing, auth gates, regression).

On the user's VPS (Windows), the listener should be able to actually connect to Telegram MTProto and the SMS-login flow (POST /api/telegram/start-login -> /api/telegram/submit-code) must be exercised once manually to persist the .session file at TELEGRAM_SESSION_PATH=/app/backend/data/telegram.session. After that, the channel 'RentaTrade Z VIP' must be set via POST /api/telegram/config {channels: ['RentaTrade Z VIP']}.

Optional UX: expose a frontend page to drive the SMS flow + display the live status (configured/authorized/connected/channels) + a 'Shadow mode ON/OFF' toggle. The 6 config fields are already PATCHable independently.

Optional: when parser returns is_signal=true but the message contains both a 'BUY' and a numeric '-' delimiter that the regex fallback misreads (e.g. 'BUY XAUUSD ENTRY 4340 - 4337'), make sure the LLM path is reached (works fine in current tests because EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is set).
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/services/telegram_copy_trader.py: process_message uses await on a non-async insert path when telegram_signals_col already has a unique index on (chat_id, message_id) — the find_one anti-dup pre-check is fine but the insert can still race under high-throughput. Consider catching DuplicateKeyError and ignoring it instead of the pre-check (idempotent + atomic).

/app/backend/services/telegram_copy_trader.py: '_resolve_mt5_symbol' returns the symbol_hint unchanged when MT5 is disconnected — downstream get_price/place_order will then fail with a generic error. Consider returning None when disconnected so the rejection reason is explicit ('mt5_disconnected') instead of 'no_tick'.

/app/backend/services/signal_parser.py: '_fallback_regex_parse' detects symbol via 'BUY|SELL|... + token' but the RentaTrade msg has 'BUY XAUUSD' on the SAME line, so the regex relies on a non-greedy match. Tested OK with current sample, but messages where the side keyword is on a separate line from the ticker will be missed by the fallback. The LLM path handles this — just be sure to keep EMERGENT_LLM_KEY set in production.

/app/backend/services/signal_parser.py: '_normalize_symbol' uses 'startswith' fallback which can mis-map e.g. 'GOLDEN' -> 'XAUUSD'. Probably fine in practice but a stricter check (exact alias OR a curated list) would be safer.

/app/backend/server.py: '/api/telegram/start-login' bubbles ALL Telethon exceptions as HTTP 500 with raw stringified detail. Consider catching ConnectionError/OSError specifically and returning a more actionable error (e.g. 'telegram_unreachable'). The Telethon AuthKeyUnregisteredError is currently surfaced raw to clients.
/app/backend/server.py: '/api/telegram/test-parse' has no rate-limit and calls Claude Sonnet 4.5 on each invocation -> cost surface. Consider a per-user rate limit or a cap on len(text).
/app/backend/server.py is now 1452 lines (>2x the 700-line threshold). Splitting into routers/{auth,bot,trades,mt5,ws,costs,backtest,telegram}.py is overdue (flagged since iteration 1).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is healthy: 91/91. Telegram module is wired correctly. On the sandbox, Telethon CANNOT connect to Telegram (AuthKeyUnregisteredError is EXPECTED and must NOT be treated as a bug) — therefore /api/telegram/status returns connected=False, authorized=False and /api/telegram/start-login returns 500. All other Telegram endpoints (status, config GET/POST, signals, test-parse) work and persist correctly. The parser uses Claude Sonnet 4.5 via emergentintegrations + EMERGENT_LLM_KEY (set in /app/backend/.env). On VPS Windows, the user must call POST /api/telegram/start-login -> /api/telegram/submit-code once to create the .session file. Admin: admin@trading.bot / Trading2025!. Local backend URL: http://localhost:8001. NEVER call the user's VPS via EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL.
rca_of_issue: No bug discovered this iteration. The new Telegram copy-trading module is correctly implemented: routes exist under /api/telegram/*, all are auth-gated via get_current_user (JWT), config persists in MongoDB collection telegram_state (single doc upsert pattern), signals listing reads from telegram_signals with status filter and a hard 200 cap on limit, and the parser correctly handles RentaTrade format (entry range -> midpoint 4338.5, TP1 numeric + TP2='OUVERT' runner=true, confidence>=0.8 from LLM), non-signal chat, and SELL+GOLD->XAUUSD alias. Backend startup is resilient: Telethon failure during connect_and_maybe_start is caught and logged as WARNING, FastAPI continues to serve.
